string.text: Official Brief on Fish

OFFICIAL BRIEF
March 1981
Commercial use of the Chernobyl NPP cooling pond
 
The inquiry has established the following:
 
1. Management of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant organized fish farming in the cooling pond.
2. The pond is contaminated with radionuclides.
3. The catch is transferred to the Ivankiv fish-processing plant.
4. From there, it enters the retail network for sale to the public.
 
Add these findings to the inquiry into the conduct of plant management.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Fish from a contaminated pond was sold to residents as ordinary food.%c[0,170,170,170]
Brief on Work Stoppages

INFORMATION BRIEF
Pripyat, 1978
Conditions within construction organizations
 
Spontaneous collective refusals to carry out assigned work have been recorded at several organizations engaged in building the city.
 
Workers cite two principal causes: wages paid late and bonuses distributed unfairly.
 
Information on the stoppages has been added to materials concerning attitudes among construction workers.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The city was still being built by people who had not been paid the money they earned.%c[0,170,170,170]
Special Report on the Bread Supply

SPECIAL REPORT
Pripyat, summer 1980
Provision of bread to the population
 
Interruptions in bread deliveries to shops and the poor quality of products from the Pripyat bakery are causing public dissatisfaction.
 
Spontaneous gatherings of residents have been observed in the city. Complaints concerning the bakery and supply organizations are being voiced in conversation.
 
State security bodies have conducted preventive measures to forestall mass demonstrations.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The report treated the people speaking out as the danger, not the bad bread.%c[0,170,170,170]
Collective Housing Petition

TO THE PRESIDIUM OF THE SUPREME SOVIET OF THE USSR
TO THE CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF THE CPSU
 
COLLECTIVE PETITION
1981
 
We, the undersigned employees of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, ask that compliance with our employment contracts and the allocation of housing in Pripyat be investigated.
 
We believe that apartments are being assigned in violation of our contracts and that living space is being distributed unfairly. We request an inquiry and notification of its findings.
 
Enclosure: signature sheets — approximately 160 signatures.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]To be heard, the workers had to appeal above both city and plant management.%c[0,170,170,170]
Water Supply Brief

BRIEF
Pripyat, 1982
Water supply in residential buildings
 
Residents continue to complain about inadequate water service. The situation is being discussed both at work and at home.
 
Because dissatisfaction persists, operational reports note the emergence of “unhealthy attitudes.”
 
Preventive measures have been taken.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The report calls the residents' attitudes “unhealthy,” not the pipes or the water.%c[0,170,170,170]
Staff and Agent Summary

STAFF AND AGENT SUMMARY
Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and the city of Pripyat
 
Year Agents Trusted Contacts
1983 46 97
1984 58 116
1985 70 98
1986 90 119
 
The Pripyat city department has increased its staff from six officers to nine. Operations are conducted under the Atom, Radium, Pripyat, and Contour plans.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]In 1986, nine officers handled 209 agents and trusted contacts.%c[0,170,170,170]
Tribuna Energetika Clipping

TRIBUNA ENERGETIKA
April 25, 1986
 
A CELEBRATION OF LABOR
 
More than 22,000 residents of Pripyat took part in the citywide Leninist volunteer workday on April 19.
 
Employees of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant and city enterprises produced goods and provided services worth more than 100,000 rubles. The city's construction organizations completed work worth more than 220,000 rubles.
 
GIVING IT THEIR ALL
 
In a single shift, a construction brigade poured thirty cubic meters of concrete.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]This issue went to press on April 25, 1986.%c[0,170,170,170]
Clipping with a Catfish Photograph

TRIBUNA ENERGETIKA
April 25, 1986
Photograph from the back page
 
A CATCH FIT FOR THE HALL OF HONOR
 
The photograph shows a young Pripyat resident with a catfish weighing approximately twenty kilograms.
 
Also on this page:
“SPAWNING SEASON”
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Friday's edition still found room for a twenty-kilogram catfish.%c[0,170,170,170]
Working Notes for an Article

WORKING NOTES
for the article “NO PRIVATE MATTER”
March 1986
 
— Review state construction standards.
— Compare the requirements with the actual condition of materials at the sites.
— Information and Computing Center: permitted to work with printouts for fifteen minutes. Stayed about thirty. Printouts may not be removed — copy the figures by hand, memorize the rest.
— At one enterprise, as much as seventy percent of output is classified as defective. Verify the calculation again.
— Prepare the piece for publication in late March.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Local authorities did not respond after the article was published.%c[0,170,170,170]
Extract from the Residential Plan

EXTRACT FROM THE RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN
City of Pripyat
 
The city plan makes no provision for individually built housing.
 
Employees of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, construction organizations, and city enterprises are housed in apartment buildings and dormitories.
 
Existing detached residence: the private home of construction director Vasily Kizima.
 
No private-housing sector is planned as the city expands.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The plan for a city of apartment blocks contained one house built for a single family.%c[0,170,170,170]
A Schoolgirl Letter Carrier's Notebook

PAGE FROM A SCHOOL NOTEBOOK
Tetiana Rosetska, ninth grade
 
After school — the post office. The telegrams must be delivered before evening. I know the city better than the map in our classroom now: almost every building and almost every entrance.
 
Sometimes I have to read an address several times because people write in a hurry. But Pripyat is small. I always find the right entrance eventually.
 
School again tomorrow. Then the post office.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]A ninth-grader knew nearly every doorway in the city because she carried people's urgent news.%c[0,170,170,170]
Draft Driver Evaluation

MOTOR TRANSPORT ENTERPRISE
DRAFT EVALUATION
 
The employee committed a traffic violation.
 
Given his youth and the need to strengthen his sense of personal responsibility, it is recommended that he be assigned community duties. Consider him for membership in the Komsomol.
 
Submit the evaluation for discussion by the work collective.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The young enterprise had fewer than ten Komsomol members; rule-breakers were urged to join.%c[0,170,170,170]
Motor Pool Dispatch Calculation

MOTOR POOL DISPATCH CALCULATION
Morning transport for shift personnel
 
Routes:
Pripyat — Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant
Pripyat — Jupiter Factory
 
Estimated workforce: approximately 17,000.
Main transport window: 1 hour.
Required buses: approximately 100.
 
Dispatch vehicles in convoys. A delay on one run increases the load on later buses and disrupts the delivery of shift personnel.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Nearly seventeen thousand people had to be moved in a single morning hour.%c[0,170,170,170]
Letter from Pripyat's “Broadway”

Hello,
 
You asked where we go on weekends. On Saturdays, almost the whole city gathers along the central promenade. We call it “Broadway.”
 
That is where they hold the market too. There is no such thing as a quick shopping trip: every few steps you meet somebody from the plant, the school, or the next building. By the time you have greeted everyone, half the day is gone.
 
People usually dress the children in their best clothes. Perhaps because there are hardly any other places here where you can meet so many people at once.
 
Otherwise, everything is the same. We work. We wait for an apartment.
 
Write back.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Even an ordinary trip to the market unfolded before the eyes of the entire city.%c[0,170,170,170]

THEATER PROGRAM

Notes on a Ukrainian-Language Class

DRAFT NOTES
Late 1970s
Opening a class taught in Ukrainian
 
No such classes remain in Pripyat's schools. A new class requires written requests from parents.
 
Ten requests received. Not enough to open a class.
 
After discussion with the principal: do not raise the matter again. Stop collecting requests.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Ten requests from parents never became a classroom.%c[0,170,170,170]
Back of an Apartment Photograph

INSCRIPTION ON THE BACK OF A PHOTOGRAPH
Pripyat, 1983
 
“Finished the graphite stack in Unit 4. Everyone came to our apartment after work.
 
That is Alexei Ananenko and Leonid Toptunov in the picture, with the others. We brought in chairs from every room, but it was still cramped. We listened to Vysotsky.”
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The city restaurant had not opened yet, so major jobs were celebrated at home.%c[0,170,170,170]
Raketa Ticket to Kyiv

PASSENGER TICKET
Raketa hydrofoil
 
Route: Pripyat — Kyiv
Service: daily
Journey time: approximately 2 hours
Boarding: city pier
 
Retain this ticket until the end of the journey.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Two hours by river separated Pripyat from Kyiv.%c[0,170,170,170]
City Skating Rink Notice

NOTICE
 
OPEN-AIR CITY SKATING RINK
 
The rink is open to the public now that the ice has been laid.
 
Please keep order, stay off the ice during maintenance breaks, and do not leave children unattended.
 
The time of the next ice service will be announced separately.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Pripyat flooded an open-air skating rink every winter.%c[0,170,170,170]
Energetik Volunteer Work Sheet
Caption for the Children's Clinic

PHOTOGRAPH FOR THE CITY ARCHIVE
Pripyat, 1984
 
CHILDREN'S CLINIC
 
Taken from a clinic window. Baby carriages left by parents during appointments stand in several rows before the building. Almost no space remains along the wall.
 
For reference: the average age of Pripyat's residents is approximately twenty-six. Hundreds of children are born in the city every year.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]There was almost no room left for another carriage outside the children's clinic.%c[0,170,170,170]
Note About a Lost Ring

April 1986
 
I lost my wedding ring at work. I searched the entire confectionery shop and never found it.
 
The woman who collects the leftover food said losing a ring means losing your fate.
 
I told Vasya. He only waved it away: “Do not listen to nonsense.” Our holiday starts next week. We will visit our parents, and I will forget all about it.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Lyudmila Ignatenko lost her ring about a week before the accident.%c[0,170,170,170]
Pripyat Civil Registry Reminder

PRIPYAT CIVIL REGISTRY OFFICE
REMINDER FOR APRIL 26, 1986
 
Several young couples are scheduled to register their marriages on Saturday. The newlyweds are to arrive at the appointed times.
 
After registration, they should lay flowers at the city monument. Wedding celebrations should preferably be held without alcoholic drinks.
 
On Sunday, prepare for the ceremonial registration of newborns.
 
Completion notes: ___________________________
 
%c[255,238,153,26]In the same businesslike hand, the reminder lists weddings and the registration of newborns.%c[0,170,170,170]
Request to Release Two Footballers

TO THE MANAGEMENT OF THE CHERNOBYL NUCLEAR POWER PLANT
 
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Employee participation in a scheduled match
 
Please release Serhii Semykopov and Viktor Ponomariov from their work shift so they may play in a scheduled fixture for the Budivelnyk football team.
 
Their wages are to be maintained for the time absent.
 
Decision: ____________________
Signature: ___________________
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Semykopov earned twenty-five rubles per match — one tenth of his monthly wage at the plant.%c[0,170,170,170]
Working Note on a Hockey Team

WORKING NOTE
Pripyat, 1986
Establishment of a city hockey team
 
1. Nine players from Siberia have been selected to relocate and begin training.
2. The transfer of a team from Kyiv's advanced sports school is under consideration.
3. A project director has been appointed.
4. Preliminary estimates have begun for an ice palace to provide permanent training and match facilities.
 
Next review: __________________________________
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The team was already taking shape. The concrete and steel for its future rink had only begun to be counted.%c[0,170,170,170]
Pripyat Radio Club Log

COLLECTIVE RADIO STATION LOG
 
1980
The first collective station, UK5UAJ, opens at School No. 3. Supervisor: A. K. Fomichev, chief designer at the Jupiter Factory.
 
1981
Collective station UK5UCU begins operating from the Energetik Palace of Culture.
 
1986
Collective stations — 2.
Individual stations — 12.
Operators attached to UK5UCU — 35–40.
Schoolchildren — 20–30.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]By 1986, fourteen amateur radio stations were operating in Pripyat.%c[0,170,170,170]
Open Radio Day Plan

EVENT PLAN
May 7 — Radio Day
 
1. Set up the collective station's equipment outdoors.
2. Conduct public radio contacts.
3. Explain call signs, signal range, and contact procedure to spectators.
 
For reference:
The radio club makes approximately 5,000 contacts each year. It offers technical and sporting programs as well as an English-language group.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The English-language group met at the radio club, not at a school.%c[0,170,170,170]
1985 Radio Expedition Log

EXPEDITION LOG
July 10–21, 1985
Ust-Orda Buryat Autonomous Okrug
 
Objective: establish an amateur radio station in an area that has never had its own call sign.
 
Completed:
— station established;
— contacts made with other regions;
— confirmation cards prepared.
 
Result: one blank spot has been removed from the country's amateur-radio map. Equipment prepared for return to Pripyat.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]One fewer blank spot remained on the map.%c[0,170,170,170]
Children's Events Plan

EVENT PLAN
April 26–27, 1986
 
April 26
Young Pioneer gathering for School No. 3 at the Palace of Culture. Expected attendance: approximately 1,500 children. Arrange assembly and conduct the planned program.
 
April 27
Children's fitness run. Prepare the route and gathering points. Responsible personnel are to verify readiness before the event begins.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]About fifteen hundred children were expected at Saturday's gathering.%c[0,170,170,170]
Brief on a Canceled Disco

INFORMATION BRIEF
Pripyat, October 6, 1985
Public action by a group of young residents
 
After a scheduled disco was canceled, a group of young residents assembled in the city and demanded that the dance be restored.
 
The gathering developed into an open protest.
 
The informal name preserved among the participants: “the battle for the disco.”
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The cancellation of a single night of dancing provoked an open protest.%c[0,170,170,170]
Letter About Fights with Construction Crews

Hello,
 
More crews have arrived for the construction projects. The workers are housed in dormitories, and the locals and newcomers cannot seem to leave each other alone. First they argue; then, after the shift, they fight again.
 
The city keeps growing, and there are more people every day, but that does not make them know one another. Do not tell Mother — she will decide it happens every evening. It is usually quiet. People simply try to learn who is local and who has just arrived before anything else.
 
Write and tell me how things are there.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]New buildings appeared faster than established residents could grow used to their new neighbors.%c[0,170,170,170]
Leaflet for Dormitory Residents

TO THE RESIDENTS OF PRIPYAT'S DORMITORIES
 
The city's twenty-four dormitories house 9,460 people.
 
A total of 136 individual complaints and three collective complaints concerning living conditions have already been submitted to various authorities.
 
We propose that residents assemble and demand concrete measures to improve those conditions.
 
The time and place of the meeting will be announced later.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The KGB named Jupiter employee V. I. Yashchenko as the organizer and prevented a mass gathering.%c[0,170,170,170]
Transcript Fragment About Furniture

KOMSOMOL CONFERENCE
TRANSCRIPT FRAGMENT
 
SPEAKER, A TEACHER:
 
“Young specialists are being assigned rooms and apartments without essential furniture or refrigerators. I ask the representatives of the city administration to say when these goods will be supplied.”
 
The question was referred to representatives of the city administration.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Wardrobes and refrigerators arrived the next day. Afterward, the speaker waited for the KGB to visit.%c[0,170,170,170]

Invitation to a Closed Disco

Submit the music program to the Department of Culture for advance approval. Works not included on the approved list may not be played during the evening.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Even a list of songs for dancing had to pass inspection first.%c[0,170,170,170]

Alexander Akimov Traffic Accident Brief

ROAD TRAFFIC ACCIDENT BRIEF
Several months before April 1986
 
Driver: Alexander Akimov.
 
The car left the roadway and fell from a bridge. A passenger in the vehicle suffered a broken arm.
 
The incident was recorded as a traffic accident. There is no evidence of other serious consequences.

Amusement Park Opening Plan
Back of a May Day Photograph

INSCRIPTION ON THE BACK OF A PHOTOGRAPH
 
Pripyat
May 1, 1975
 
City schoolchildren during the May Day celebration. A festive column on one of the new streets.
 
The children's names are not recorded.
 
Series: construction and the first years of life in Pripyat.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The city was five years old on the day this picture was taken.%c[0,170,170,170]
Report on the Canteen-Site Explosion

INDUSTRIAL ACCIDENT REPORT
Pripyat, February 28, 1984
Site: canteen under construction
 
The commission has established that an explosion occurred during construction work.
 
Worker Mikhail Anulenko was killed. Seven others suffered injuries of varying severity.
 
A criminal case has been opened. The investigation is to determine the circumstances of the explosion and whether safety requirements were observed.
 
Commission members' signatures: ______________
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The criminal case preserved the name of a man who never returned from his shift.%c[0,170,170,170]
Equipment Theft Brief

INQUIRY BRIEF
Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, 1983
 
The theft of equipment and material assets worth more than 60,000 rubles has been established.
 
The materials have been forwarded for investigation and identification of those involved in removing the property from the plant.
 
Storage and accounting procedures for material assets, as well as the current access-control system, are to be reviewed.
 
Prepared by: ____________________
 
%c[255,238,153,26]Even after the loss was confirmed, those responsible still had to be found.%c[0,170,170,170]
Rumor: Two Hanged Young Men

Hello,
 
You asked what people here say about those two boys. Everyone repeats the same thing: two young men were supposedly found hanged in Pripyat in 1974.
 
Nobody could give me their names or say where it happened. The person who told me heard it from somebody else. Do not put too much faith in it, and do not tell the children.
 
In a small city, somebody else's words quickly become the truth.
 
Unsigned letter.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]No confirmed record of this incident has been found.%c[0,170,170,170]
Rumor: The Girl from Dormitory No. 10

Circa 1984
 
People are talking about Dormitory No. 10 again. They say a young woman was murdered there. Nobody seems to know who she was or what happened.
 
I asked around discreetly. Everyone repeats the same story, but no one has seen a document or even a newspaper item.
 
Do not write to Mother about it. She already thinks a dormitory is the most frightening place in the world. Perhaps everyone will have forgotten the story by next week.
 
Write back.
 
%c[255,238,153,26]The story survives only as an urban rumor; no documentary confirmation has been found.%c[0,170,170,170]
